JURJANI-DALAIL: In the comparison with وجعلوا الجن شركاء لله, the stated order makes partners specific to jinn; fronting شركاء broadens the meaning to deny any partner, yielding more meaning in fewer words. | mentions 6:100 JURJANI-DALAIL: Fronting can preserve a word's grammatical role, as when a predicate or object is moved before its subject, or can transfer it into a new role. JURJANI-DALAIL: In a second kind of fronting, word order changes grammatical roles: المنطلق زيد makes المنطلق the subject, while زيد ضربته makes زيدا a subject and the verb's object a pronoun. {"id": "28:77/q15", "question": "What inward corruption is warned against?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q15/p1", "position": "Misusing spiritual potential against religious law corrupts the land of the spirit.", "reasons": "Al-Bursawī transmits the Najmī interpretation: following nature damages human and spiritual preparedness."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q16", "question": "What can fī al-arḍ attach to?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q16/p1", "position": "It may depend on tabghi, al-fasād, or an omitted circumstance.", "reasons": "Al-Samīn calls the omitted circumstantial analysis remote."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q17", "question": "Which earth is meant by in the earth?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q17/p1", "position": "The land inhabited by Qārūn's people, a part of the globe.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr says corruption in that area counts as corruption within the earth as a whole."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q18", "question": "Why is earth singular here and elsewhere?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q18/p1", "position": "It denotes the lower realm or a collective abode, rather than counted earths.", "reasons": "Al-Zarkashī contrasts earth with the plural heavens in 65:12: their distinct entities suit a plural, while earth is the lower realm, like a pebble beside a desert. He calls earth this world's abode; one view excludes the heavens from the world. Heaven too is singular for encompassing height, as in 67:16-17 and 10:61, but plural in 34:3 for full dominion. A hadith of wrongful land taking treats seven earths as countable tracts."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q19", "question": "What does God's not loving corrupters mean?", "turns_on": "Whether lack of love is expressed as rejection of deeds and favor or as lack of nearness.", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q19/p1", "position": "God rejects their acts and does not approve, favor or honor them.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās mentions deeds and practice; al-Bayḍāwī attributes divine dislike to evil acts. Al-Biqāʿī denies worldly prosperity proves divine favor. Ibn ʿĀshūr says the clause explains the ban; Islahi likens corrupters to weeds destined for removal."}, {"id": "28:77/q19/p2", "position": "God does not draw near to corrupters.", "reasons": "Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna's lā yaqrub; al-Māwardī attributes it to Ibn Qutayba."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q20", "question": "What does divine dislike imply about willing corruption?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q20/p1", "position": "God does not will corruption; if He created it, He would will it.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī uses the clause to refute the Mujabbira account of creation and will."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q21", "question": "Who delivered the admonition to Qārūn?", "turns_on": "Whether the plural counsel is attributed to believing kinsmen or Moses.", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q21/p1", "position": "Believers among Qārūn's people or kinsmen addressed him.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabrisī calls this usual; al-Ālūsī says it is the verse's apparent sense. Kur'an Yolu describes believers enlightened by faith; Islahi calls them learned men."}, {"id": "28:77/q21/p2", "position": "Moses addressed him, in the plural form.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf, al-Ṭabrisī, al-Rāzī and al-Ālūsī report this alternative."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q22", "question": "Why did Qārūn fail to heed the counsel?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q22/p1", "position": "Admonition could not benefit one denied acceptance, and Qārūn answered with ingratitude.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī compares advice to seed on saline ground; al-Rāzī calls the counsel unimprovable but says Qārūn claimed wealth came from his own knowledge."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q23", "question": "What happened during Qārūn's sinking?", "turns_on": "The reports recount different episodes and grounds for his sinking or its halt.", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q23/p1", "position": "The earth swallowed him at Moses' prayer; Qārūn appealed to Moses through kinship, not directly to God.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī says Moses continued commanding the earth to take him."}, {"id": "28:77/q23/p2", "position": "When Jonah's fish reached Qārūn, God stopped his sinking because he asked about Moses.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī says the fish circled the seas and God credited Qārūn's kinship concern."}]}
{"id": "28:77/q24", "question": "What did Qārūn believe?", "turns_on": "Whether the religious counsel and divine gift presuppose belief.", "positions": [{"id": "28:77/q24/p1", "position": "He acknowledged the afterlife and was an Israelite monotheist, yet doubted Moses' promises and prescriptions.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī infers an acknowledged afterlife from the counsel; Ibn ʿĀshūr describes his religious affiliation and doubt."}, {"id": "28:77/q24/p2", "position": "He was an unbeliever who nevertheless received worldly blessings.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī says an unbeliever has no good deed in the relevant sense but may receive worldly gifts."}]}
